text:
oncall-bot: PAGERS: high error rate detected on edge-proxy/us-west-2 - spike in 502/504 + TLS handshake failures (alert id: EDGE-TLS-1937654321). Please acknowledge if oncall.

marie: acked. I'm current oncall for infra. seeing ~18% 5xx at the edge for the last 4m. dashboards -> 502 and 504, plus logs show 'tls: handshake failure' and 'alert: untrusted client' for some connections.

ashok: I'm on pages too. first check: are we rotating client certs for mutual TLS this morning? folks ran cert rotation job at 03:00 UTC per release notes.

marie: checking rotation job logs... `kubectl -n infra logs job/cert-rotate-2026-03-14` shows exit code 0 but I see a couple of failures in downstream sync to proxy nodes. past hour's certs: new cert expiry 2027-03-14 - looks fine.

jordan: grabbing raw edge logs: `grep "handshake" /var/log/edge/*.log | tail -n 50` -> a lot of `tls: received unexpected handshake message` and `client certificate signature verification failed`.

kai: @marie can you run `openssl s_client -connect proxy-usw2.example.net:443 -showcerts` from a healthy jump host and from a failing host? I want to verify the cert chain the proxy is presenting vs what clients expect.

marie: from jump-1 (healthy region): output shows certificate chain with intermediate CA A, leaf CN=proxy-usw2, Valid from 2026-03-13 to 2027-03-13. From failing host (edge-node-7): same leaf, but chain truncated - intermediate missing. `Verify return code: 21 (unable to verify the first certificate)`.

ashok: truncated chain -> likely a bad upload of intermediate cert to some nodes during the rotation sync. that would explain handshake failures when clients require full chain validation.

emily: customer impact: Callouts from support: three enterprise customers reported 50-60% request failures starting ~02:50 UTC. Our global traffic routing sent many of their traffic to us-west-2.

support-bot: Noted support tickets: T-1492, T-1493, T-1494. Affected services: playground, embeddings. Priority P1 for customers in tickets.

marie: immediate mitigation plan: 1) Force re-upload missing intermediate to all edge nodes; 2) temporarily enable local fallback to present alternate full-chain from central cert store; 3) shift traffic away from problematic nodes/hosts (drain edge-node-7/8/9). Going to run the re-upload now.

jordan: how to re-upload? we have helper script: `scripts/deploy_certs.sh --target edge --certs=central-store/2026-03-13/chain.pem` it uses the rolling agent. Suggest run with `--parallel 3` to limit impact.

marie: running `scripts/deploy_certs.sh --target edge --certs=central-store/2026-03-13/chain.pem --parallel 3` now. watching logs.

sre-bot: Deploy started by marie on 3 hosts in parallel. rollout id: rollout-1937654321-1.

marie: progress: nodes 1-9 updated. node-7 had an error syncing to local certdir: `permission denied` on `/etc/ssl/chain.pem`. digging.

ashok: node-7 permission denied -> maybe ansel agent ran with changed umask after last config change. Can you `ssh` and inspect?

marie: on node-7: `ls -l /etc/ssl` shows owner root:root but file was created by ansible user earlier; file perms `rw-------`. agent was trying to write as `deploy` user -> failing. I'm changing ownership and re-running the script for node-7.

marie: re-run complete, node-7 now has full chain. rechecks: `openssl s_client` now returns `Verify return code: 0 (ok)` from both jump host and edge node.

kai: great. what's the impact on error rate?

jordan: pulling metrics -> error rate dropped from 18% to 4% across cluster in last 3 min. 502s down significantly, handshake failure logs almost gone.

emily: customer ticket updates: emailing affected customers with ETA and mitigation summary. Support will request postmortem and RFO if there is SLA exposure.

marie: follow-ups: 1) make rotation job explicitly verify chain on each host post-deploy (currently it's only spot-checked). 2) add a checksum of uploaded chain to central tracing so we can detect divergence. 3) fix agent permissions so deploy user can write certs. 4) alerting refinement - add a specific 'incomplete cert chain' alert for edge proxies.

ashok: agree. I'll own (1) and (2). plan: update rotation job to run `openssl verify -CAfile /etc/ssl/chain.pem /etc/ssl/leaf.pem` on each host and retry upload if verification fails. Also add a canary check against 10% of nodes.

marie: I'm handing primary oncall over to @kai in 10m for continued verification and to coordinate postmortem. Kai ack?

kai: ack, taking oncall. I'll keep the thread open for final closure. I'll also coordinate with platform to roll a permissions fix in the agent package.

sre-bot: Incident status changed to mitigated. Time to mitigation: ~12 minutes from first alert.

emily: quick customer impact summary for SMT: ~18% of requests in us-west-2 experienced 5xx between 02:46-02:58 UTC. Top affected customers: AcadiaCorp (30% of their requests), BrightForms (60%), internal dev org (10%). No data exposure.

support-bot: Tickets updated with mitigation notes and ETA for postmortem: 48 hours.

kai: closing checklist: confirm all nodes have chain verified, ensure rotation job fixes checked in, patch agent perm issue, draft postmortem. I will file the incident doc after handoff.

marie: Thanks team. I'll follow up with a short runbook change and the exact command snippets we used.

oncall-bot: Incident thread will remain open for 2h for any regressions. If no new alerts, please mark as resolved.

kai: marking intent to resolve in 2h if clean. thanks all for quick responses. :white_check_mark:
